name: pair_device
description:
Add/pair or remove a physical device -- callable any time.

PROTOCOL (the `protocol` argument -- lowercase: insteon, zwave, zigbee, matter, x10):
- Adding a NEW device: ask the customer which protocol it is if unclear. x10 returns a not-yet-supported message -- walk the customer through manual pairing instead.
- Removing an EXISTING device: never guess its protocol from the device's name or model. Call get_device_family (INSTEON -> insteon, Z-Wave -> zwave, Zigbee -> zigbee, Matter -> matter), or just try node_op(delete): it succeeds for insteon and is rejected for zwave/zigbee/matter/plugin with the real protocol named in the error (see DEVICES, Protocol family).
- A Z-Wave controller still running the Legacy (pre-Z-Matter) generation returns a clear error for any zwave action -- tell the customer to use the ISY administrative console for that controller.

ACTIONS:
- add_by_address (insteon/x10 only -- the only protocols with a customer-readable address): for a device whose own address the customer already knows or can read off the unit. Waits (up to ~80s) for the new device to actually become usable before returning, so it's safe to reference the returned device_address in the very next tool call.
- include (insteon/zwave/zigbee; NOT matter): opens pairing mode and waits for that protocol's own pairing session to end (however long the customer takes, up to ~80s), then returns whatever was newly discovered in its result's new_devices list (address + whatever name the hub assigned, usually blank -- no separate lookup needed; rename via node_op using that address). insteon's pairing window supports multiple devices in one call -- all of them come back in new_devices. zwave/zigbee/matter devices have no customer-readable address, so add_by_address is not valid for them and there is nothing to ask: once the customer says they want to add one, call include immediately, in this same turn, with no clarifying question or confirmation first (not even rhetorically, e.g. 'you probably don't have an address, right?') -- asking first is the stalling pattern to avoid. device_type is optional -- omit it unless the customer already volunteered it. include for matter is NOT implemented via chat (it needs a pairing/QR code this tool cannot accept) -- calling it just returns a message telling the customer to use the eisy-ui interface directly.
- exclude (zwave/zigbee/matter only -- insteon has no distinct hardware remove mode; use node_op(delete) for insteon): removes a device. Whether device_address is required depends on the protocol -- this is the one place add/remove aren't symmetric, so don't assume. For zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL and should normally be omitted -- the customer identifies the device physically (pressing its own exclude button once the hub is listening), not by name in chat, so never ask 'which device' first; this opens removal mode, waits (same ~80s budget) for the customer to activate the device, then reports which device the hub excluded in removed_devices. Only pass device_address for zwave if the customer already volunteered a specific address. For zigbee/matter, device_address IS required (from DEVICE DATABASE, never guessed) and there is no physical activation window: the call performs the ENTIRE removal immediately and returns status=exclusion_committed with removed_devices already populated -- do not tell the customer to do anything on-screen, and do not call this twice; one call is the whole operation. Zigbee can fail silently at the network layer (the hub only disables the node locally); this call detects that and returns an error (with device_address) instead of a false success -- if you get it, tell the customer the device could not be removed from the Zigbee network and they need to remove it manually from the eisy-ui interface, linking it as /nodes/{device_address} per UI NAVIGATION.

BEFORE CALLING include or a zwave exclude: these BLOCK for up to ~80s waiting for the customer's own physical action, which they do on their own screen (an on-screen dialog eisy-ui shows them), not in this chat. Say your instructions to the customer as plain text in this same reply, immediately BEFORE the tool call (e.g. 'I've put the hub in pairing mode -- follow the instructions on your screen to add the device.') -- never 'let me know when you're done' or any variant expecting a chat reply, because there won't be one; the call already waits for that to finish on its own. Text written after the tool call in your reply is what you say once it's already done.

LINKING: any device this tool adds/pairs/removes, regardless of protocol, is a device node -- when you mention it in your reply, link it as /nodes/{address} per UI NAVIGATION, using the address this tool's own result gave you (e.g. new_devices[].address). Never a /plugins/... link -- that is only ever for the plugin marketplace/dashboard/licenses, never for a device (even one a plugin created). For adding a marketplace plugin (not a physical device), use install_plugin/buy_plugin instead.

protocol.description: The device's protocol family, lowercase. Adding a new device: ask the customer if unclear. Removing an existing device: from get_device_family (INSTEON -> insteon, Z-Wave -> zwave, Zigbee -> zigbee, Matter -> matter) or a rejected node_op(delete) -- never guessed from the device's name.

action.description: add_by_address is insteon/x10 ONLY (needs device_address) -- not valid for zwave/zigbee/matter, which have no customer-readable address before pairing; use include for those instead, never ask the customer for an address. include (add) works for insteon/zwave/zigbee -- opens pairing mode and blocks until the customer completes it on their own screen (or times out), then returns new_devices directly; for matter it instead returns a message directing the customer to the eisy-ui interface, since chat-based Matter pairing isn't implemented. exclude (remove) works for zwave/zigbee/matter only -- for zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL (the customer identifies the device physically, not by name -- opens removal mode and blocks the same way as include); for zigbee/matter, device_address IS required and it performs the whole removal in this one call, immediately, no window.

device_address.description: The device's own physical address, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE -- never guessed. Required for action=add_by_address, and for action=exclude when protocol is zigbee/matter (that exact address is removed directly). NOT required for action=exclude when protocol is zwave -- omit it there; the customer identifies the device physically and the hub reports back which one was excluded.

device_type.description: Optional device-type hint (add_by_address/include). Never ask the customer for this before calling -- omit it unless they already mentioned the device type unprompted; it is not worth delaying the call for.
